# 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship, officially sponsored by JenningsBet, was a professional snooker tournament organized by World Seniors Snooker (WSS) . Held from Wednesday, May 7 to Sunday, May 11, 2025, at the iconic Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, England, the event marked a historic turning point in the senior snooker circuit , , . This edition was not merely an annual sporting competition but the last major championship staged under a long-standing, restrictive agreement between its organizer and the main professional World Snooker Tour (WST). Following the conclusion of the 2025 event, this agreement expired, leading to a fundamental reshaping of the tournament's eligibility criteria and competitive landscape , . The winner of the 2025 championship was England's Alfie Burden, who defeated Jersey's Aaron Canavan 8–4 in the final to claim the £20,000 first prize , . The tournament featured a 16-player field competing in a single-elimination knockout format, with progressively longer matches culminating in a best-of-fifteen frame final , . Its broadcast live on Channel 5 in the UK and Ireland solidified its position as a flagship 'Sheffield event' through a strategic partnership with Sheffield City Council , . The 2025 staging also represented the seventh consecutive year the championship had been hosted at the Crucible Theatre, cementing its association with one of snooker's most hallowed venues , .

## Tournament Identity and Organization

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship is a professional snooker tournament organized by World Seniors Snooker (WSS), a private limited company established on June 13, 2018 . The organization operates under the auspices of the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association (WPBSA) to provide competitive opportunities for players aged 40 and over, allowing them to extend their careers beyond the main professional World Snooker Tour , . The company's registered office is located in Bristol, United Kingdom, and its business activities are classified under SIC code 93199, 'Other sports activities', confirming its statutory role in organizing senior snooker competitions . The Chairman of World Seniors Snooker is Jason Francis, a prominent figure in the sport who also manages several top players, including former world number one Ronnie O'Sullivan , . The tournament itself is the premier event on the World Seniors Snooker Tour . For the 2025 edition, the championship was known as the JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship, indicating the sponsorship arrangement in place for that year . The event was broadcast live and exclusively in the UK and Ireland on Channel 5, ensuring wide viewership for the five-day spectacle , . The entire operation was managed by a team led by Chairman Jason Francis and Director Mike Dunn, both of whom have backgrounds as former professionals . The organization's strategic direction for 2025 included forging deeper community ties within Sheffield, such as launching a new educational partnership with Sheffield Hallam University’s Sport Business Management programme, which offered student placements across various departments involved in the event's production and promotion , . This initiative was part of a broader campaign called 'Sheffield Loves Snooker', aiming to embed the championship as a central pillar of the city's sporting calendar , .

The organizational framework of WSS has historically been defined by its contractual relationship with the World Snooker Tour (WST), the primary governing body and administrative arm of professional snooker . This relationship governed key aspects of the seniors tour, including scheduling, player eligibility, and commercial rights . However, this dynamic underwent a dramatic shift in May 2025. Following the conclusion of the World Seniors Championship, the existing agreement between WSS and WST was terminated , . According to Jason Francis, this decision was driven by failed negotiations and a lack of consultation from the WST, which had scheduled its own events, such as the Tour Championship in Hull, at the same time as the UK Seniors Championship, creating an unworkable conflict and effectively cancelling the latter . This breakaway freed WSS to operate independently, granting it the autonomy to schedule events without WST interference, invite any eligible player it chose, and negotiate its own sponsorships and broadcasting deals . This newfound freedom was immediately leveraged to implement significant changes to the tournament's rules, most notably by lowering the age limit for participation and removing the ban on players ranked within the world's top 64 , . These changes marked a paradigm shift, transforming the tournament from a platform primarily for older, non-ranking players into a potential showcase for all senior players, regardless of their current standing on the main tour. The financial structure of the 2025 championship reflected this growth, with the winner receiving £20,000 and the runner-up £10,000, a substantial increase from earlier editions and underscoring the event's growing prestige and value within the snooker ecosystem . The move to organize the event independently also allowed WSS to pursue a more ambitious tour schedule for the subsequent 2025/26 season, pledging a total prize fund of £27,000 across nine tour events, more than double the amount from the previous season .

## Historical Context and Venue Significance

The lineage of the World Seniors Snooker Championship traces back to its inaugural professional non-ranking tournament, held in 1991 . This original event was promoted by Barry Hearn and sanctioned by the WPBSA, taking place from September 18 to 22, 1991, at Trentham Gardens in Stoke-on-Trent, England , . It featured a field of 16 players aged 40 or older, competing in a single-elimination format where all rounds, including the final, were played over a best-of-nine frames basis , . Wales' Cliff Wilson emerged victorious, defeating Australia's Eddie Charlton 5–4 in the final on September 22, 1991, securing the £16,000 top prize , . The tournament was not held again until 2010, creating a 19-year hiatus during which only a few smaller-scale events, such as the 1997 Seniors Pot Black and the 2000 World Seniors Masters, took place . The modern era of the championship began in 2010 when it was revived as an annual series, initially run by Matchroom before being rebranded under the World Seniors Tour , . The 2010 revival saw Jimmy White win his first seniors title by defeating Steve Davis 4–1 at the Cedar Court Hotel in Bradford, England . The event was held annually from 2010 to 2016 (with a gap in 2014), then again in 2017 and 2018 under the banner of Snooker Legends, before being staged continuously every year from 2019 onwards . This uninterrupted annual staging since 2019 culminated in the 2025 championship, which marked the seventh consecutive year the event was held at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield , .

The selection of the Crucible Theatre as the permanent home for the World Seniors Championship from 2019 represents a significant development in the tournament's history. The Crucible, synonymous with the World Snooker Championship, lends immense prestige and a grand atmosphere to the seniors' event . The decision to establish a long-term partnership with Sheffield City Council ensured the tournament would be positioned as a flagship 'Sheffield event for Sheffield people', aligning with the council's 'Sheffield Loves Snooker' campaign , . This collaboration extended beyond mere venue booking to include community engagement initiatives such as 'Seniors of Sheffield Day' and 'Business and Youth of Sheffield Day', demonstrating a commitment to integrating the championship into the fabric of the local community , . The 2025 championship was confirmed to continue at the Crucible through at least 2027, signaling a stable and promising future for the event in its new permanent home . The progression of the tournament's format and prize structure reflects its growing stature. Initially a non-ranking event, it became a full WPBSA-sanctioned event in 2013 . Over the years, the prize fund grew, reaching £20,000 for the winner by 2025 , . The competitive format also evolved, moving from the best-of-nine frames used in the 1991 final to a tiered system seen in 2025: best-of-seven frames for the first round and quarter-finals, best-of-eleven for the semi-finals, and a best-of-fifteen frame final , , . This structure mirrors that of other major ranking tournaments, further elevating the championship's profile and providing a clear, exciting pathway to glory for the competitors. The consistent presence of legendary players like Jimmy White, who holds the record for most titles with four wins (in 2010, 2019, 2020, and 2023), has been a key factor in maintaining the event's popularity and historical significance .

## Participants and Qualification Pathways

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship featured a field of 16 elite players, representing nine different nations and competing for the prestigious title and the £20,000 first prize . The composition of the field was determined through a structured and multi-faceted qualification process, designed to reward recent form, regional success, and past achievements while also providing opportunities for newcomers , . The participants included a mix of high-profile returnees, recent retirees, seasoned veterans, and emerging talents from across the globe, making for a highly competitive and star-studded lineup , . The qualifying pathways were clearly defined, offering distinct routes to secure one of the 16 coveted spots in the main draw. The table below outlines the confirmed participants and their respective qualification methods, providing a comprehensive overview of the tournament's entry criteria.

The qualification pathways were diverse and well-defined. Firstly, the defending champion, Igor Figueiredo of Brazil, received automatic entry as the holder of the title , . Secondly, the field included several high-profile players returning to competitive action after retirement. Four-time champion Jimmy White, 1997 World Champion Ken Doherty, and two-time ranking event winner Joe Perry were among those who accepted invitations, adding significant star power and drawing attention to the tournament , . Notably, both Joe Perry and Dominic Dale made their debuts at the Crucible, having both retired from the main World Snooker Tour in April 2025 , . Thirdly, four spots were awarded to the winners of regional Seniors Championships, serving as a crucial gateway for international talent. Charl Jonck secured his place by winning the African Seniors Snooker Championship, Hassan Kerde claimed the Asia-Pacific title, Fabio Anderson Luersen triumphed in the Americas, and Craig Steadman represented Europe , , . Fourthly, four automatic qualification places were given to the top four players on the World Seniors Snooker Tour's 'Race to the Crucible' ranking list, a series of nine tour events that determines the season's form players , . This group included Aaron Canavan, the eventual finalist and reigning world number one, alongside Andrew Norman, Gerard Greene, and Wayne Townsend , . Finally, one last spot was contested in a 'Golden Ticket' Play-Off, a knockout event held at The Crucible Club in Reading on April 19–20, 2025 , . This play-off featured 16 players who qualified based on their rankings but did not secure one of the automatic spots, with the winner earning the final place in the main championship draw . This comprehensive qualification system ensured a balanced and competitive field, blending experience, recent form, and global representation.

## Tournament Stages and Final Results

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship unfolded over five days at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, following a standard single-elimination knockout format with a 16-player field , . The matches were structured to build intensity, with the opening rounds and quarter-finals contested over the best of seven frames, the semi-finals over the best of eleven frames, and the final decider set as a best-of-fifteen frames contest , , . The tournament was broadcast live on Channel 5 and 5Action in the UK, capturing the drama and skill of the competition for a national audience . The event kicked off on Wednesday, May 7, with the first-round matches, setting the stage for several major shocks and thrilling encounters . One of the most significant early exits was that of the defending champion, Igor Figueiredo of Brazil. He lost 2–4 to Wayne Townsend of England, a result that signaled the start of a competitive tournament where no seed was safe , , . Another surprise came in the first round clash between four-time champion Jimmy White and Alfie Burden. Despite White's illustrious career, he was defeated by Burden in a surprising 1–4 result, ending his hopes of equalling the record for most titles , . Similarly, 1997 World Champion Ken Doherty lost 2–4 to Charl Jonck of South Africa, while Tony Drago defeated Gerard Greene 4–3 , . The first-round victories for Joe Perry, Dominic Dale, and Tony Knowles set up a compelling quarter-final draw , .

The quarter-finals saw some of the tournament's most dramatic moments. Dominic Dale advanced with a hard-fought 4–2 victory over Craig Steadman, while Joe Perry secured his place by edging out Fabio Anderson Luersen 4–2 , . However, the most anticipated quarter-final match was between Dale and Perry, two recently retired legends. In a match that lived up to the billing, Dominic Dale fought back from 1–3 down to win 4–1, booking his place in the semi-finals . Meanwhile, Alfie Burden continued his impressive run, defeating Tony Drago 4–3 to join Dale in the last four . The semi-finals delivered even more nail-biting finishes. In a match described as tense, Aaron Canavan fought back from behind to defeat Dominic Dale 6–5, securing his spot in his second consecutive final . His opponent in the final was Alfie Burden, who had earlier defeated Hassan Kerde 6–2 , . The final, held on Sunday, May 11, 2025, was contested between the two Englishmen, Aaron Canavan and Alfie Burden , . Burden proved to be the better performer on the day, winning the match 8–4 to claim the championship title , . Post-match, Burden expressed confidence in his performance, stating he felt strong and prepared for the challenge, having expected to win the final . ## Pivotal Organizational Changes and Eligibility Rules

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship served as a watershed moment, marking the definitive end of a long-standing and restrictive agreement between its organizer, World Seniors Snooker (WSS), and the main professional World Snooker Tour (WST) , . This agreement, which had governed the seniors tour for years, imposed two critical limitations on player eligibility. Firstly, it stipulated that professional players ranked outside the world's top 64 needed to be aged 45 or over to participate in WSS events , . Secondly, and more significantly, it barred players who were currently ranked within the world's top 64 from competing in any WSS tournament , . This latter restriction effectively excluded the highest echelon of active players, including members of the celebrated 'Class of 92'—Ronnie O'Sullivan, Mark Williams, and John Higgins—who, despite being over the age threshold, were prevented from participating due to their current rankings , . The agreement also contained clauses that restricted WSS's operational autonomy, preventing it from scheduling events that clashed with the WST calendar or pursuing independent sponsorship and broadcasting arrangements . The expiration of this contract after the conclusion of the May 2025 championship fundamentally altered the competitive landscape of senior snooker.

Following the termination of the agreement, World Seniors Snooker Chairman Jason Francis announced a series of immediate and transformative rule changes. The most profound of these was the lifting of the ban on top-64 players. As of May 2025, any player aged 45 and above was now eligible to compete in WSS events, provided their participation did not create a scheduling conflict with a WST event , , . This opened the door for a host of marquee names to potentially appear in future seniors tournaments. The first tangible beneficiary of this change was Matthew Stevens, a former World Championship runner-up who was 47 years old and ranked 52nd in the world , . He promptly entered the British Seniors Open in Derby, which was televised on Channel 5 over Christmas 2025, becoming the first top-64 player to compete in a WSS event under the new rules , . Francis explicitly stated that the commercial terms, rather than eligibility, were now the sole barrier to 'Class of 92' members like Ronnie O'Sullivan, Mark Williams, and John Higgins appearing at future Crucible-based World Seniors Championships , . This development signals a potential influx of the sport's biggest stars into the seniors circuit, dramatically increasing its appeal and competitiveness.

In addition to lifting the top-64 ban, the age eligibility requirements were also revised for the 2025/26 season and beyond. The minimum age for amateur players was lowered from 45 to 40 , . While the 45+ requirement remained for former professionals who were outside the top 64 of the main tour, the overall accessibility of the tour was significantly increased , . This change meant that players who had recently turned 40 could immediately compete in WSS events, broadening the talent pool considerably. This policy shift raised concerns among some observers about the potential dilution of the event's original purpose, which was to provide a platform for older players with limited opportunities on the main tour . Indeed, for the 2025 championship itself, at least 13 of the 16 confirmed participants were under the age of 45, highlighting the impact of the new rules . The combination of a lower age limit and the removal of the top-64 exclusion created a far more open and competitive environment. The new regulations aimed to attract younger, more skilled senior players while simultaneously creating the possibility of featuring established superstars, thereby enhancing the quality and marketability of the World Seniors Snooker Tour. This strategic pivot represents a bold new chapter for the organization, moving away from its previous constraints to embrace a more inclusive and commercially viable future.

## Broader Implications and Future Outlook

The termination of the agreement with the World Snooker Tour and the subsequent implementation of sweeping eligibility changes mark a defining moment for the future of the World Seniors Snooker Championship and the broader senior circuit , . The most immediate and tangible implication is the significant enhancement of the tournament's competitive depth and commercial potential. By opening the doors to players ranked inside the world's top 64, WSS has created the possibility of featuring the sport's most famous and successful players in its events . The debut of Matthew Stevens at the British Seniors Open was a landmark moment, proving that the new rules are already bearing fruit . With commercial terms now identified as the primary hurdle, the prospect of seeing "Class of 92" legends like Ronnie O'Sullivan, Mark Williams, and John Higgins compete at the Crucible becomes increasingly plausible, which would undoubtedly boost viewership, attract new sponsors, and elevate the status of the seniors tour to unprecedented levels . This shift transforms the championship from a nostalgic gathering of past greats into a genuine battleground where current and former world-class talent can compete on a level playing field, judged purely on merit.

To capitalize on this new era of opportunity, World Seniors Snooker has committed to a substantial investment in the sport's infrastructure and prize structure. For the forthcoming 2025/26 season, the organization announced a pledge to deliver a total prize fund of £27,000 across its nine-tournament tour, a sum more than double that of the previous season . Furthermore, the prize money for individual tour events was doubled to £1,000, and prize money will now be paid out to the last 16 players in each event, significantly widening the financial incentive for a larger field of competitors . This financial commitment, coupled with the expanded eligibility, signals a clear strategy to professionalize and grow the senior circuit. The expansion of the age limit to 40+ for amateurs and the inclusion of all former professionals over 45 will attract a younger and more dynamic cohort of players, fostering greater competition and raising the overall standard of play , . The introduction of Super Seniors events on Sundays for players over 55 further diversifies the tour, catering to a wider range of experienced athletes . This multi-pronged approach aims to create a sustainable and thriving ecosystem for senior snooker, providing meaningful competitive opportunities throughout the season.

Despite this newfound independence and ambition, certain strategic decisions reflect a pragmatic approach to the tour's logistical realities. A notable constraint remains the venue for the WSS tour events themselves. While the premier World Seniors Championship continues its successful tenure at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, the nine regular tour events scheduled for the 2025/26 season will all be held at the Crucible Sports and Social Club in Reading , . This choice, cited by Jason Francis as economically unviable to expand internationally, means that continental qualifiers must travel to Reading to compete for ranking points, a logistical challenge that may limit the global reach of the tour compared to its aspirations . However, this centralized model ensures consistency and allows WSS to leverage its established relationships and facilities at the Reading venue. In summary, the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship stands as a pivotal event that successfully navigated its final days under the old regime while simultaneously launching a new, more ambitious, and commercially attractive era for the sport. The future outlook is one of significant growth, characterized by enhanced player eligibility, increased prize money, and the tantalizing prospect of witnessing the world's greatest snooker players compete in the senior ranks once again.

Craig Steadman of Europe was a Golden Ticket Play-Off Winner.
Hassan Kerde of Asia-Pacific was a Continental Champion (Asia-Pacific).
Charl Jonck of Africa was a Continental Champion (Africa).
Fabio Anderson Luersen of Americas was a Continental Champion (Americas).
The qualification pathways were diverse and well-defined.
The defending champion, Igor Figueiredo of Brazil, received automatic entry as the holder of the title.
The field included several high-profile players returning to competitive action after retirement.
Four-time champion Jimmy White, 1997 World Champion Ken Doherty, and two-time ranking event winner Joe Perry were among those who accepted invitations.
Their participation added significant star power and drew attention to the tournament.
Both Joe Perry and Dominic Dale made their debuts at the Crucible.
They had both retired from the main World Snooker Tour in April 2025.
Four spots were awarded to the winners of regional Seniors Championships.
These served as a crucial gateway for international talent.
Charl Jonck secured his place by winning the African Seniors Snooker Championship.
Hassan Kerde claimed the Asia-Pacific title.
Fabio Anderson Luersen triumphed in the Americas.
Craig Steadman represented Europe.
Four automatic qualification places were given to the top four players on the World Seniors Snooker Tour's 'Race to the Crucible' ranking list.
The 'Race to the Crucible' is a series of nine tour events that determines the season's form players.
This group included Aaron Canavan, the eventual finalist and reigning world number one.
The group also included Andrew Norman, Gerard Greene, and Wayne Townsend.
One last spot was contested in a 'Golden Ticket' Play-Off.
The play-off was a knockout event held at The Crucible Club in Reading on April 19–20, 2025.
This play-off featured 16 players who qualified based on their rankings but did not secure one of the automatic spots.
The winner earned the final place in the main championship draw.
This comprehensive qualification system ensured a balanced and competitive field, blending experience, recent form, and global representation.
The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship unfolded over five days at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield.
It followed a standard single-elimination knockout format with a 16-player field.
The matches were structured to build intensity.
The opening rounds and quarter-finals were contested over the best of seven frames.
The semi-finals were contested over the best of eleven frames.
The final decider was set as a best-of-fifteen frames contest.
The tournament was broadcast live on Channel 5 and 5Action in the UK.
The broadcast captured the drama and skill of the competition for a national audience.
The event kicked off on Wednesday, May 7, with the first-round matches.
The first-round matches set the stage for several major shocks and thrilling encounters.
One of the most significant early exits was that of the defending champion, Igor Figueiredo of Brazil.
Igor Figueiredo lost 2–4 to Wayne Townsend of England.
This result signaled the start of a competitive tournament where no seed was safe.
Another surprise came in the first round clash between four-time champion Jimmy White and Alfie Burden.
Despite White's illustrious career, he was defeated by Burden in a surprising 1–4 result.
This defeat ended White's hopes of equaling the record for most titles.
1997 World Champion Ken Doherty lost 2–4 to Charl Jonck of South Africa.
Tony Drago defeated Gerard Greene 4–3.
The first-round victories for Joe Perry, Dominic Dale, and Tony Knowles set up a compelling quarter-final draw.
The quarter-finals saw some of the tournament's most dramatic moments.
Dominic Dale advanced with a hard-fought 4–2 victory over Craig Steadman.
Joe Perry secured his place by edging out Fabio Anderson Luersen 4–2.
The most anticipated quarter-final match was between Dale and Perry, two recently retired legends.
In a match that lived up to the billing, Dominic Dale fought back from 1–3 down to win 4–1.
Dominic Dale booked his place in the semi-finals.
Alfie Burden continued his impressive run, defeating Tony Drago 4–3 to join Dale in the last four.
The semi-finals delivered even more nail-biting finishes.
In a match described as tense, Aaron Canavan fought back from behind to defeat Dominic Dale 6–5.
Aaron Canavan secured his spot in his second consecutive final.
His opponent in the final was Alfie Burden.
Alfie Burden had earlier defeated Hassan Kerde 6–2.
The final, held on Sunday, May 11, 2025, was contested between the two Englishmen, Aaron Canavan and Alfie Burden.
Burden proved to be the better performer on the day, winning the match 8–4 to claim the championship title.
Post-match, Burden expressed confidence in his performance, stating he felt strong and prepared for the challenge.
Burden expected to win the final.

Tony Drago defeated Gerard Greene 4–3 in the First Round on May 8, 2025.
Hassan Kerde defeated Tony Knowles 4–0 in the First Round on May 8, 2025.
Dominic Dale defeated Joe Perry 4–1 in the Quarter-Final on May 9, 2025.
Alfie Burden defeated Tony Drago 4–3 in the Quarter-Final on May 9, 2025.

Aaron Canavan defeated Andrew Norman 4–1 in the Quarter-Final on May 9, 2025.
Aaron Canavan defeated Dominic Dale 6–5 in the Semi-Final on May 10, 2025.
Alfie Burden defeated Hassan Kerde 6–2 in the Semi-Final on May 10, 2025.
Alfie Burden defeated Aaron Canavan 8–4 in the Final on May 11, 2025.
The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship served as a watershed moment.
It marked the definitive end of a long-standing and restrictive agreement between its organizer, World Seniors Snooker (WSS), and the main professional World Snooker Tour (WST).
This agreement had governed the seniors tour for years.
It imposed two critical limitations on player eligibility.
Firstly, it stipulated that professional players ranked outside the world's top 64 needed to be aged 45 or over to participate in WSS events.
Secondly, it barred players who were currently ranked within the world's top 64 from competing in any WSS tournament.
This latter restriction effectively excluded the highest echelon of active players.
Members of the celebrated 'Class of 92'—Ronnie O'Sullivan, Mark Williams, and John Higgins—were prevented from participating due to their current rankings, despite being over the age threshold.
The agreement also contained clauses that restricted WSS's operational autonomy.
It prevented WSS from scheduling events that clashed with the WST calendar.
It prevented WSS from pursuing independent sponsorship and broadcasting arrangements.
The expiration of this contract after the conclusion of the May 2025 championship fundamentally altered the competitive landscape of senior snooker.
Following the termination of the agreement, World Seniors Snooker Chairman Jason Francis announced a series of immediate and transformative rule changes.
The most profound of these was the lifting of the ban on top-64 players.
As of May 2025, any player aged 45 and above was now eligible to compete in WSS events.
This was provided their participation did not create a scheduling conflict with a WST event.
This opened the door for a host of marquee names to potentially appear in future seniors tournaments.
The first tangible beneficiary of this change was Matthew Stevens.
Matthew Stevens is a former World Championship runner-up.
Matthew Stevens was 47 years old and ranked 52nd in the world.
He promptly entered the British Seniors Open in Derby, which was televised on Channel 5 over Christmas 2025.
Matthew Stevens became the first top-64 player to compete in a WSS event under the new rules.

Francis explicitly stated that the commercial terms, rather than eligibility, were now the sole barrier to 'Class of 92' members like Ronnie O'Sullivan, Mark Williams, and John Higgins appearing at future Crucible-based World Seniors Championships.
This development signals a potential influx of the sport's biggest stars into the seniors circuit.
This would dramatically increase its appeal and competitiveness.
In addition to lifting the top-64 ban, the age eligibility requirements were also revised for the 2025/26 season and beyond.
The minimum age for amateur players was lowered from 45 to 40.
The 45+ requirement remained for former professionals who were outside the top 64 of the main tour.
The overall accessibility of the tour was significantly increased.
This change meant that players who had recently turned 40 could immediately compete in WSS events.
This broadened the talent pool considerably.
This policy shift raised concerns among some observers about the potential dilution of the event's original purpose.
The original purpose was to provide a platform for older players with limited opportunities on the main tour.
For the 2025 championship itself, at least 13 of the 16 confirmed participants were under the age of 45.
This highlights the impact of the new rules.
The combination of a lower age limit and the removal of the top-64 exclusion created a far more open and competitive environment.
The new regulations aimed to attract younger, more skilled senior players.
The new regulations aimed to create the possibility of featuring established superstars.
This would enhance the quality and marketability of the World Seniors Snooker Tour.
This strategic pivot represents a bold new chapter for the organization.
The organization is moving away from its previous constraints to embrace a more inclusive and commercially viable future.

The termination of the agreement with the World Snooker Tour and the subsequent implementation of sweeping eligibility changes mark a defining moment for the future of the World Seniors Snooker Championship and the broader senior circuit.
The most immediate and tangible implication is the significant enhancement of the tournament's competitive depth and commercial potential.
By opening the doors to players ranked inside the world's top 64, WSS has created the possibility of featuring the sport's most famous and successful players in its events.
The debut of Matthew Stevens at the British Seniors Open was a landmark moment.
It proved that the new rules are already bearing fruit.

With commercial terms now identified as the primary hurdle, the prospect of seeing "Class of 92" legends like Ronnie O'Sullivan, Mark Williams, and John Higgins compete at the Crucible becomes increasingly plausible.
This would undoubtedly boost viewership, attract new sponsors, and elevate the status of the seniors tour to unprecedented levels.

This shift transforms the championship from a nostalgic gathering of past greats into a genuine battleground where current and former world-class talent can compete on a level playing field, judged purely on merit.
To capitalize on this new era of opportunity, World Seniors Snooker has committed to a substantial investment in the sport's infrastructure and prize structure.
For the forthcoming 2025/26 season, the organization announced a pledge to deliver a total prize fund of £27,000 across its nine-tournament tour.
This sum is more than double that of the previous season.
Furthermore, the prize money for individual tour events was doubled to £1,000.
Prize money will now be paid out to the last 16 players in each event.
This significantly widens the financial incentive for a larger field of competitors.
This financial commitment, coupled with the expanded eligibility, signals a clear strategy to professionalize and grow the senior circuit.
The expansion of the age limit to 40+ for amateurs and the inclusion of all former professionals over 45 will attract a younger and more dynamic cohort of players.
This will foster greater competition and raise the overall standard of play.
The introduction of Super Seniors events on Sundays for players over 55 further diversifies the tour.
This caters to a wider range of experienced athletes.
This multi-pronged approach aims to create a sustainable and thriving ecosystem for senior snooker.
It provides meaningful competitive opportunities throughout the season.
A notable constraint remains the venue for the WSS tour events themselves.

While the premier World Seniors Championship continues its successful tenure at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, the nine regular tour events scheduled for the 2025/26 season will all be held at the Crucible Sports and Social Club in Reading.
This choice was cited by Jason Francis as economically unviable to expand internationally.
This means that continental qualifiers must travel to Reading to compete for ranking points.
This presents a logistical challenge that may limit the global reach of the tour compared to its aspirations.
However, this centralized model ensures consistency.
It allows WSS to leverage its established relationships and facilities at the Reading venue.
In summary, the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship stands as a pivotal event.
It successfully navigated its final days under the old regime.
It simultaneously launched a new, more ambitious, and commercially attractive era for the sport.
The future outlook is one of significant growth.

This growth is characterized by enhanced player eligibility, increased prize money, and the tantalizing prospect of witnessing the world's greatest snooker players compete in the senior ranks once again.

2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship Dates
---------------------------------------------

### When is the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship?

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship gets underway on Wednesday 7th May, two days after the conclusion of the 2025 World Snooker Championship, and runs through until Sunday 11th May.

2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship Venue
---------------------------------------------

### Where is the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship taking place?

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship will be held at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, with the fabled venue now synonymous with the event.

Previously being staged in cities such as Stoke-on-Trent, Peterborough and Blackpool, Sheffield has been the competition's home since 2019, meaning the 2025 staging will be the seventh successive year that it will have been held there.

2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship Age Limit
-------------------------------------------------

### What is the age limit to play at the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship?

The minimum age for players on the main tour but outside the top 64 was reverted to 45 years ahead of the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship, whilst the minimum age for amateur players remained at 40.

In the past the minimum age limit has varied between both 40 and 45.

2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship Players
-----------------------------------------------

### Who is playing at the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship?

Sixteen players have been confirmed to feature at the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship, including defending champion Igor Figueiredo.

Four-time event winner Jimmy White is also amongst the field as are former ranking event champions Ken Doherty, Dominic Dale and Joe Perry, both of whom officially retired from the professional stage earlier this year.

### Who has the most World Seniors Snooker Championship wins?

Jimmy White is the most decorated player in World Seniors Snooker Championship history, winning the prestigious tournament on four occasions.

In total, 'The Whirlwind', who famously lost all seven of his World Snooker Championship finals, has reached the final on six occasions, losing just two of them.

His most recent triumph came in 2023 when he saw off Alfie Burden in the showpiece, having previously reigned supreme in 2020, 2019 and 2010.

History of the World Seniors Snooker Championship
-------------------------------------------------

### When was the first World Seniors Snooker Championship?

The World Seniors Snooker Championship was launched back in 1991 when Welshman Cliff Wilson edged past Australian Eddie Charlton in dramatic fashion in Stoke-on-Trent.

That was the one and only occasion it took place prior to 2010 however, when the World Seniors Tour was re-branded and relaunched, with greater prize money, helping to attract higher profile players including Jimmy White.

Since 2010, the event has been staged every year, with the exception of 2014.

### How does the World Seniors Snooker Championship work?

A single game of snooker is known as a frame, with the winner being decided by which player has scored the most points by the time all the balls have been potted on the table or if there are not enough points available for the player that is trailing to be able to mount a comeback.

Most snooker matches at professional level are contested over more than just a one-frame format.

For example the first round of the World Seniors Snooker Championship will be played over a best-of-seven frame format, essentially meaning the first player to four frames is the winner.

Matches in the quarter-finals remain over the same length, before they expand to best-of-11 in the semi-finals and then best-of-15 in the showpiece final.

### How many frames are played in World Seniors Snooker Championship games?

First-round matches are the best-of-seven frames contests, the same length as the four quarter-final ties. Semi-finals then expand to a best-of-11 format before the final is played out over 15 frames.

*   Final - Best-of-15 frames
*   Semi-Finals - Best-of-11 frames
*   Quarter-Finals - Best-of-seven frames
*   Last 16 - Best-of-seven frames

### How much will the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship winner get?

The prize money for the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship will remain unchanged from 2024 with the winner set to receive £20,000 and the runner-up taking home a cool £10,000.

Jason Francis recently shared some important information about the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship:

**[World Seniors Snooker Announces Partnership with Sheffield Hallam University](https://seniorssnooker.com/world-seniors-snooker-announces-partnership-with-sheffield-hallam-university/)**
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

> **World Seniors Snooker (WSS) is delighted to announce a ground breaking new partnership with Sheffield Hallam University which will see students currently studying Sport Business Management get real time experience working on the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship.**
> 
> The initiative was launched yesterday by WSS Chairman Jason Francis and Director Mike Dunn with opportunities offered for students to experience every aspect of producing, promoting, planning and executing a major sporting TV event.
> 
> WSS are offering placements alongside their industry professionals for students to experience how staging a major sporting event in the city at the iconic Crucible Theatre with a live television production team comes together.
> 
> ![Image 1](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-3.png?w=771)
> 
> Chairman of World Seniors Snooker Jason Francis said “_World Seniors Snooker has entered into a long term partnership with Sheffield Council to make the World Seniors Snooker Championship an event to showcase everything that is great about the Steel City. A Sheffield event for Sheffield people which engages with their ‘Sheffield Loves Snooker’ campaign. The energy and enthusiasm we got from the students yesterday proved to me that they can play a real part in making this year’s Championship the best ever. The work with Sheffield Hallam is the latest initiative which will sit alongside our Business and Youth of Sheffield Days and the continuation of Seniors of Sheffield Day. I am really looking forward to working with, but also learning from, them_.”
> 
> Dr Ruth M Crabtree, Head of the School of Sport & Physical Activity said “_We are delighted to be collaborating with the World Seniors Snooker. When you think of Sheffield and sport, you instantly think of snooker and this partnership is a great opportunity for our students to gain real world experience of working on a major iconic sport event and learn from experienced professionals. At Sheffield Hallam, our mission is to be the world leading applied university, and we pride ourselves on working with major sport organisations within Sheffield, the region and globally. The collaboration will allow students to work within sport marketing, media, public relations and event management, gaining key skills needed within sport management, helping enhance their CV, increase their network, and gain valuable expertise. We believe we are sector leading in offering value added opportunities for our students and it is always great to them jump ay the chance to volunteer for such initiatives. I am extremely confident our students will learn a lot and also some innovative and creative ideas to Jason Fracnis and his team at World Seniors Snooker._”
> 
> Nathan Withey, a third year Sport Business Management Student, said “_My time at Sheffield Hallam University has been filled with opportunities to improve my professionalism and to make sure I have experience when starting my career after graduation. What I’m most excited about for the World Senior Snooker Championship is the opportunity to gain valuable insight into how an event of this magnitude is created. What it takes to be involved, and the skills required to produce a sporting event which I can hopefully learn to harness though this opportunity. I am very much looking forward to working with the team and I am grateful for the opportunity_.”
> 
> ![Image 2](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-4.png?w=1024)
> 
> The World Seniors Snooker Championship starts on Wednesday 7 May and runs until Sunday 12 with snooker legends Jimmy White, Ken Doherty and Tony Drago confirmed alongside Seniors Champions from Pan-America, Pan-Asia, Europe and Africa and more. The event will be shown live and exclusively in the UK and Ireland on Channel 5.

**Format Change Announced for 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship**
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

> **World Seniors Snooker (WSS) is pleased to announce a change to the format of the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship which will take place at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield on 7-11 May.**
> 
> All rounds up to and including the quarter-finals will now be the best-of-seven frames, while the semi-finals will now best best-of-11 frames and the final will be contested over the best-of-15 frames.
> 
> ![Image 3](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-5.png?w=1024)
> 
> Brazil’s Igor Figueiredo made history for South America by winning the flagship title last May and he will open proceedings on the opening Wednesday afternoon. Jimmy ‘The Whirlwind’ White, a record four-time champion, and two-time runner-up Ken Doherty are both set to begin their campaigns on the afternoon of Thursday 8 May.
> 
> [**Tickets remain available for the World Seniors Championship and start from just £17.50.**](https://www.sheffieldtheatres.co.uk/events/world-seniors-snooker-championship-2025)

I can’t really comment on the first announcement other than stating the obvious: Seniors snooker is determined to stay in Sheffield and to get involved in various projects that will benefit the city, its inhabitants and the Seniors circuit. What’s not to like?

Regarding the second announcement … longer matches, yes, that’s good news to me. It’s also a sign that the seniors involved nowadays in the competition are better than those who played in the “early” instalments of the Seniors World Championship[1](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/03/19/news-about-the-2025-world-seniors-snooker-championship/#c4a4e1a5-5240-46aa-9c74-120e9a8a6d62). One of the reason the matches were so “short” is because the frames tended to be long. Some of the legends involved really struggled to make telling breaks and weren’t really physically fit. Frames tended to last rather long …

Don’t get me wrong: they had every right to be there, they gave it their all and the crowd gave them a very warm support. They promoted the event with all their might and heart. It wouldn’t exist without them and what they did to promote it.

But the event has evolved. The seniors who now compete in it are younger and much fitter. Therefore, it is now reasonable – and desirable – to lengthen the matches a bit. I’m sure that the fans won’t complain!

1.  In his current form, under Jason Francis’ management. [↩︎](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/03/19/news-about-the-2025-world-seniors-snooker-championship/#c4a4e1a5-5240-46aa-9c74-120e9a8a6d62-link)

When is the World Seniors Snooker Championship 2025?
----------------------------------------------------

The World Seniors Snooker Championship 2025 will get underway on **Wednesday, May 7.**

This is just **TWO** days after the conclusion of the World Snooker Championship, which sees Chinese star [Zhao Xintong take on Welshman Mark Williams](https://www.thesun.co.uk/sport/34785907/world-snooker-championship-2025-live-results-zhao-williams-final-updates/) in the final.

The tournament will be aired on Channel 5 in the UK and can be live streamed on My5.

Sadly, the World Seniors Snooker Championship 2025 only runs for five days, finishing on **Sunday, May 11.**

Crucible Theatre in Sheffield is the chosen venue as is the case every year.

[SunSport has live coverage of the whole event](https://www.thesun.co.uk/sport/34798032/world-seniors-snooker-championship-2025-live-results-jimmy-white/).

What has been said?
-------------------

There had been doubts about whether the World Seniors Snooker Championship 2025 would remain at The Crucible.

But the questions have been answered and it is positive news.

Chairman of World Seniors Snooker, Jason Francis said “It’s great news to confirm our Championship will be staying in Sheffield at the Crucible.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Our strategic partnership with the council allows the World Seniors Snooker to showcase everything that is great about Sheffield.

“This year as well as repeating our Seniors of Sheffield Day we are running a Business and Youth of Sheffield Day alongside our work with Sheffield Hallam University.”

Order of Play for 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship Announced
===============================================================================

11th April 2025

[Home](https://seniorssnooker.com/) » Order of Play for 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship Announced

**The order of play for the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship has been confirmed following yesterday’s draw made live on Channel 5.**

The event will take place at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield on 7-11 May with 16 players from nine nations competing for the flagship title on the World Seniors Snooker tour.

![Image 4](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/SeniorsDraw-300x169.jpg)

Every ball will be available to watch live on Channel 5 in the UK with a new, extended format announced for the 2025 edition of the competition which sees all matches up to the semi-finals stage now being best of seven frames while the semi-finals are now best of 11 and the final contested over the best of 15 frames.

The tournament begins on Wednesday afternoon with former ranking event champions Joe Perry and Dominic Dale making their respective World Seniors Snooker bows against Brazil’s Fabio Anderson Luersen and England’s Craig Steadman.

![Image 5](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/wednesday-8th-may-300x300.jpg)

Reigning champion Igor Figueiredo will begin the defence of his crown against Crucible debutant Wayne Townsend on Wednesday evening to be followed by fellow former World Seniors Snooker champion Aaron Canavan taking on Andrew Norman.

In what is sure to be a highly anticipated session on Thursday afternoon, four-time champion Jimmy ‘The Whirlwind’ White meets the winner of the upcoming Golden Ticket play-off before 1997 world champion Ken Doherty goes head-to-head with African Seniors champion Charl Jonck.

![Image 6](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/thursday-8th-may-300x300.jpg)

The opening round then concludes on Thursday evening with Tony ‘The Tornado’ Drago from Malta taking on Northern Ireland’s Gerard Green before Tony Knowles meets Australia’s Hassan Kerde.

The final will take place on Sunday 11 May.

[**Tickets remain available for the World Seniors Championship and start from just £17.50.**](https://www.sheffieldtheatres.co.uk/events/world-seniors-snooker-championship-2025)

Following his stint in the commentary box and television studio as a pundit for the BBC during its coverage of the 2025 World Snooker Championship, Ken Doherty is set to return to competitive action on the baize himself this week.

![Image 1](https://www.totallysnookered.com/jpim-static/image/2025/04/17/11/05/GettyImages-79752621.jpeg?trim=0,28,0,28&crop=&width=640&quality=65&enable=upscale)![Image 2: placeholder image](https://www.totallysnookered.com/img/placeholder.jpg)

Getty Images

Irishman Doherty - who began as the pre-tournament favourite with the title sponsors - [is part of a cosmopolitan 16-player field in Yorkshire](https://www.totallysnookered.com/sport/snooker/seniors-snooker/2025-world-seniors-snooker-championship-full-draw-results-format-match-schedule-how-to-watch-5115892). His first round match is against South Africa’s Charl Jonck - who qualified by winning the African Seniors Snooker Championship - on Thursday afternoon.

Doherty can be very content with his illustrious career which has seen him win six ranking titles, including the sport’s blue riband event - the World Professional Snooker Championship - in 1997 when he stopped world number one and reinging champion Stephen Hendry’s 29-match winning streak in the final.

However, ‘The Darlin’ of Dublin’ surely has a burning desire to win the World Seniors Snooker Tour’s flagship tournament, and in the process complete a unique, never-done-before quadruple of world titles having already won the world under-21, amateur, and professional accolades.

In 1989, Doherty secured the World Under-21 Snooker Championship that was held in Reykjavik, Iceland.

Doherty defeated Peter Lines and Troy Shaw in the quarter and semi-finals respectively before facing Jason Ferguson - the current Chairman of the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association - in the title match, which he won 11-5.

A few months later in Singapore, Doherty notched up a historic double as he also won the World Amateur Snooker Championship.

Players representing 10 different nations/regions were defeated by him en route to the title, with Doherty recording an 11-2 victory over Jonathan Birch in the final.

The following year, Doherty entered the professional ranks, where he has stayed ever since.

In his rookie season, Doherty navigated several qualifying matches to reach the Crucible where he met six-time world champion Steve Davis in round one.

He went 4-0 down before going on to lead 7-5 and 8-6, although Davis emerged as a 10-8 victor.

His next trip to the Crucible was in 1994 when he defeated Alex Higgins and Alan McManus to score his first match wins there, before bowing out 13-10 to Jimmy White in the quarter-finals.

In 1995 he lost first round, in 1996 he got to round two, but 12 months later he dispatched Mark Davis, Steve Davis, John Higgins, Alain Robidoux, and then Hendry in the final to scoop snooker's ultimate prize.

Just like the under-21 and amateur crowns he won in 1989, Doherty was also the first Irishman to win this particular title.

No previous winner of the world professional title had won either the under-21 (event began in 1987) or amateur (first won in 1963) world title before, so Doherty wrote himself into the record books for that, too.

Twenty-eight years later, Doherty is now going for more history as he tries to capture the world seniors title at the Crucible.

It is a title that Doherty has come agonisingly close to before.

In 2020, he reached the final and had one hand and several fingers on the trophy as led White 4-0 in the best-of-nine title match. However, after the mid-session interval, defending champion White produced a stunning comeback, stringing together five consecutive frames for a 5-4 win.

Last year, Doherty made the final again, and began very well with a break of 100 in the opening frame, but he had to settle for the runner-up spot once more as Brazil's Igor Figueiredo ran out a 5-2 winner.

As mentioned earlier, Doherty still plys his trade on the professional circuit. At the qualifiers for the recent World Professional Snooker Championship, Doherty eliminated Haydon Pinhey 10-3 in the opening qualifying round before going out to David Lilley - World Seniors Snooker Champion in 2021 - in the subsequent round.

**18+ Be Gamble Aware**

Line-Up Confirmed for 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship
=========================================================================

8th April 2025

[Home](https://seniorssnooker.com/) » Line-Up Confirmed for 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship

**Jimmy White, Ken Doherty and Igor Figueiredo headline a star-studded line-up at the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Championship which takes place at the Crucible Theatre on 7-11 May.**

![Image 4](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/D52_0411-300x200.jpg)

Brazil’s Figueiredo made history for South American snooker 12 months ago by winning the flagship title and he will begin the defence of his crown as the top seed on the opening Wednesday afternoon session.

Jimmy ‘The Whirlwind’ White will be aiming to win a record-extending fifth World Seniors Snooker Championship title at the sport’s most iconic venue and he gets underway on the afternoon of Thursday 8 May – as does the 1997 World champion Ken Doherty.

![Image 5](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/White2-300x200.jpg)

Former ranking event champions Joe Perry and Dominic Dale will make their World Seniors Snooker debuts at the event and they are joined as seeds by Malta’s Tony ‘The Tornado’ Drago, former world number two Tony Knowles and World Seniors Snooker’s world number one Aaron Canavan – who notably won the 2018 Championship.

Canavan is one of four players to have qualified via the ‘Race to the Crucible Series’ which saw players compete across nine events to earn their spots via the rankings. The man from Jersey is joined by Andrew Norman, Gerard Greene and Crucible debutant Wayne Townsend in qualifying via this route.

![Image 6](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/WS-Snooker-Poster-2025-FINAL-212x300.jpg)

Additionally, Craig Steadman, Hassan Kerde, Charl Jonck and Fabio Anderson Luersen will add to the international field having earned their right via the continental Seniors Championships in the Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa and Americas regions respectively.

One place remains up for grabs and this will go to the winner of the ‘Golden Ticket’ Play-Off which sees 16 players competing for the spot at The Crucible Club in Reading on 19-20 April. Click here to view the draw.

[**Tickets remains available for the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship and start from £17.50.**](https://www.sheffieldtheatres.co.uk/events/world-seniors-snooker-championship-2025)

World Seniors
=============

**World Seniors Snooker (WSS) was established by the WPBSA in June 2018 to provide opportunities for players over 40 to be able to extend their snooker careers beyond the professional World Snooker Tour.**

From the former greats of the professional sport including world champions who have still got the desire to play competitively, to talented amateurs who still crave the opportunity to live their snooker dreams, the WSS Tour provides opportunities for senior players around the world.

Since 2020, tournaments have for the first time also been open to current professional players ranked outside of the world’s top 64, providing a direct link to the World Snooker Tour.

![Image 4](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/FergusonFrancis-1-1024x683.jpg)

Governing Body Support
----------------------

WSS is a subsidiary organisation of snooker’s world governing body the WPBSA and is also a full member of snooker’s international federation the World Snooker Federation.

Through these fundamental links WSS is a key organisation within the infrastructure of professional snooker and is able to provide a clear pathway to prestigious competitions for successful players. In recent years these have included places at major tournaments including the Champion of Champions and professional World Championship qualifiers.

![Image 5](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/WSF-World-Seniors-Partnership-Logo.jpg)

WSS Directors
-------------

The WSS board is run on a day-to-day basis by its Board of Directors, under the governance of the WPBSA.

*   [Jason Francis](https://seniorssnooker.com/staff/jason-francis/) – Chairman

The televised action from the Crucible Theatre isn’t over just yet, as the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship takes place on the sport’s grandest stage across five days between Wednesday 7th to Sunday 11th May.

![Image 15: Credit: Andy Chubb](https://www.totallysnookered.com/jpim-static/image/2024/05/12/14/02/Igor%20Figueiredo%202024%20World%20Seniors%20Andy%20Chubb.jpg.jpg?trim=0,0,0,0&crop=&width=640&quality=65&enable=upscale)![Image 16: placeholder image](https://www.totallysnookered.com/img/placeholder.jpg)

Credit: Andy Chubb | ANDY CHUBB

Who is playing in the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship and how did the draw work? Round one preview
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Over the past season, players from across the globe have been trying to qualify via various routes for the main draw and join the invited players.

Eight cueists were seeded with their names fixed into the bracket. These were: Figueiredo, Aaron Canavan, Dominic Dale, Joe Perry, Jimmy White, Tony Drago, Tony Knowles and Doherty.

The other eight players were then randomly drawn against the seeds for round one.

Figueiredo will begin his title defence against England’s Wayne Townsend, who qualified via the seniors tour’s one-year list and is preparing for his debut on snooker’s grandest stage.

Four-time World Seniors Snooker Champion Jimmy White - three of those title triumphs came at the Crucible in 2019, 2020 and 2023 - will face the winner of the Golden Ticket event and fellow Londoner Alfie Burden in a repeat of the final from two years ago.

No player other than White has won this title more than once.

Ken Doherty has reached this final twice before, but is still aiming to create snooker history by becoming the first player to have won world junior, amateur, professional, and seniors championships.

The Irishman plays South Africa’s Charl Jonck, the reigning African Seniors Snooker Champion.

Multiple-time world ranking event winners Joe Perry and Dominic Dale both recently retired from the professional circuit, but neither player is hanging up their cue just yet, as they have both accepted invites to this year’s seniors extravaganza.

Both will be making their seniors debuts and would play each other in the quarter-finals if they get past Brazil's Fabio Luersen (Pan American Seniors Champion) and England's Craig Steadman (European Seniors Champion) respectively in round one.

In all-qualifier tie, winner of this title in 2018 Jersey's Canavan meets Andrew Norman - who nearly eliminated White in round one last year - while former world number two Tony Knowles shares the baize with Australia's Hassan Kerde, the current Asia-Pacific Seniors Champion.

Malta's quick cueman Tony Drago has impressed on his last two visits to the Championship reaching the semi-finals on both occasions. The former top 16 star is back and has been drawn against former World Games gold medallist and qualifier Gerard Greene.

2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship Draw/Results:

### Round One

Igor Figueiredo (Brazil) 2-4 **Wayne Townsend (England)**

**Aaron Canavan (Jersey)** 4-1 Andrew Norman (England)

**Dominic Dale (England)** 4-2 Craig Steadman (England)

Fabio Luersen (Brazil) 2-4 **Joe Perry (England)**

Jimmy White (England) 1-4 **Alfie Burden (England)**

**Tony Drago (Malta)** 4-3 Gerard Greene (Northern Ireland)

**Hassan Kerde (Australia)** 4-0 Tony Knowles (England)

**Charl Jonck (South Africa)** 4-2 Ken Doherty (Ireland)

### Quarter-Finals

Townsend 2-4 **Canavan**

**Dale** 4-1 Perry

**Burden** 4-3 Drago

**Kerde** 4-2 Jonck

### Semi-Finals

**Canavan** 6-5 Dale

**Burden** 6-2 Kerde

### Final

Canavan 4-8 **Burden**

**2025 WORLD SENIORS SNOOKER CHAMPION: ALFIE BURDEN (**[**Report**](https://www.totallysnookered.com/sport/snooker/seniors-snooker/crucible-glory-for-alfie-burden-as-he-wins-the-2025-world-seniors-snooker-championship-5122707)**)**

What is the format, what are the match lengths?
-----------------------------------------------

Only one table will be in operation throughout the tournament. The event is straight knockout.

*   **First round and quarter-finals:** Best of 7 frames
*   **Semi-finals:** Best of 11 frames
*   **Final:** Best of 15 frames

Who are the referees at the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship?
--------------------------------------------------------------------

A team of four will referee at the Crucible for the televised event:

*   Michaela Tabb
*   Proletina Velichkova
*   Mark Beale
*   Rod Eaton

Velichkova - from Bulgaria - is set to officiate the final.

How can I watch the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship?
------------------------------------------------------------

Channel 5 in the United Kingdom will provide live coverage throughout the five-day tournament.

Afternoon sessions will be broadcast on the Channel 5 main channel, and 5 Action will screen the evening sessions.

Channel 5’s online streaming service “5” will also show the matches.

Sheffield Hallam cues up partnership with World Seniors Snooker
===============================================================

[Sport](https://www.shu.ac.uk/news/all-articles/latest-news?tagFilter={1CF43DCB-6DC4-490D-B48E-DAB31D6D45DA}) [Student stories](https://www.shu.ac.uk/news/all-articles/latest-news?tagFilter={031C314C-D749-4497-B482-A7E638E2C55F}) [Education](https://www.shu.ac.uk/news/all-articles/latest-news?tagFilter={0293E552-E9A8-4DCA-9DC1-851E809032BF})

**Sheffield Hallam University and World Seniors Snooker have announced a ground-breaking new partnership which will see students currently studying Sport Business Management get real time experience working on the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship.**

**Press contact:** Jo Beattie | [j.beattie@shu.ac.uk](mailto:j.beattie@shu.ac.uk)

![Image 2: A group of people stood on a set of steps outside a Sheffield Hallam University building](https://www.shu.ac.uk/-/media/home/news/world-seniors-snooker.jpg?iar=0&hash=C072F086D4BB2D00D231B6FCED3B4105)

The initiative was launched by World Seniors Snooker Chairman Jason Francis and fellow director, and former snooker professional, Mike Dunn with opportunities offered for students to experience every aspect of producing, promoting, planning and executing a major sporting TV event.

World Seniors is offering placements alongside their industry professionals for students to experience how staging a major sporting event in the city, at the iconic Crucible Theatre, with a live television production team comes together.

**Dr Ruth M Crabtree, Head of the School of Sport and Physical Activity at Sheffield Hallam University, said:** “We are delighted to be collaborating with World Seniors Snooker. When you think of Sheffield and sport, you instantly think of snooker and this partnership is a great opportunity for our students to gain real world experience of working for a major iconic sport event and learn from experienced professionals.  Our mission is to be a leading applied university, and we pride ourselves on working with major sport organisations within Sheffield, the region and globally.

“We believe we are sector leading in offering value added opportunities for our students and it is always great to see them jump at the chance to volunteer for such initiatives.  I am confident our students will learn a lot and offer some innovative and creative ideas.”

The collaboration will allow students to work within sport marketing, media, public relations, and event management, gaining key skills needed within sport management, helping enhance their CV, increase their network, and gain valuable expertise.

**Nathan Withey, third-year Sport Business Management Student, said:** “My time at Sheffield Hallam University has been filled with opportunities to improve my professionalism and to make sure I have experience when starting my career after graduation.  What I’m most excited about for the World Senior Snooker Championship is the opportunity to gain valuable insight into how an event of this magnitude is created. What it takes to be involved, and the skills required to produce a sporting event which I can hopefully learn to harness though this opportunity.  Very much looking forward to working with the team and grateful for the opportunity."

**Chairman of World Seniors Snooker Jason Francis said**: “Seniors Snooker has entered into a long-term partnership with Sheffield Council to make the World Seniors Snooker Championship an event to showcase everything that is great about the Steel City. A Sheffield event for Sheffield people, engaging with their ‘Sheffield Loves Snooker’ campaign. The energy and enthusiasm we got from the students proved to me that they can play a real part in making this year’s Championship the best ever. The work with Sheffield Hallam is the latest initiative which will sit alongside our ‘Business’ and ‘Youth’ of Sheffield Days and the continuation of ‘Seniors of Sheffield’ day. I’m really looking forward to working with, but also learning from, them.”

The Championship starts on Wednesday 7 May with Snooker Legends Jimmy White, Ken Doherty and Tony Drago.

Seniors Snooker
===============

**World Seniors Snooker (WSS) operates under the auspices of the WPBSA to provide opportunities for players over 40 to be able to extend their snooker careers.**

The WPBSA clearly recognises that there is a demand from many amateurs and the former greats of the professional sport who have still got the desire to play snooker competitively. The World Seniors Snooker Tour therefore provides an important facility by which retiring players from the professional World Snooker Tour will still be able to compete.

![Image 4:  ](https://wpbsa.com/wp-content/uploads/Seniors-logo-600x600.png)

These events also carry a great nostalgia, evoking memories of great sporting moments that we have witnessed in snooker that have created the legends in our sport. Nobody will forget the first ever maximum 147 break made at the Crucible made by Canada’s Cliff Thorburn back in 1983 and so to see him lift the trophy at the same venue some 35 years later last month was a truly special moment.

More information on the WSST can be found at the [official World Seniors website.](https://www.seniorssnooker.com/)[](https://www.facebook.com/WorldSeniorsSnooker/ "Visit Disability Snooker Facebook")

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship – Semi-Finals
=========================================================

[May 11, 2025May 11, 2025](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/05/11/the-2025-world-seniors-snooker-championship-sfs/) [seniorsnooker](https://seniorsnooker.com/author/seniorsnooker/) [Uncategorized](https://seniorsnooker.com/category/uncategorized/)

Today’s final at the Crucible will be competed between two players who have been here before: Aaron Canavan, who won the title in 2018, and Alfie Burden who was runner-up in 2023.

[Here is how the semi-finals unfolded as reported by WSS](https://seniorssnooker.com/burden-and-canavan-set-up-world-final-meeting/):

> **Burden and Canavan Set Up World Final Meeting**
> -------------------------------------------------
> 
> **Alfie Burden and Aaron Canavan will meet in the final of the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship on Sunday afternoon.**
> 
> The two former finalists reached the title match by overcoming Hassan Kerde and Dominic Dale respectively on a memorable semi-final Saturday at the iconic Crucible Theatre.
> 
> ![Image 1](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image.png?w=1024)
> 
> Canavan heads into the title match aiming to become only the second multiple champion of the most prestigious event in seniors snooker, after four-time winner Jimmy White, while Burden hopes to go one step further than he did in 2023 when he ended as runner-up to ‘The Whirlwind’.
> 
> Former professional Burden and Asia-Pacific Seniors champion Kerde, from Australia, kicked off a bumper session with a best-of-11 frame contest.
> 
> ![Image 2](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-1.png?w=1024)
> 
> Burden was in fine form and he wasted no time in racing into a 4-0 lead with breaks of 57 and 65. The Australian briefly rallied, taking back-to-back frames to half the deficit, but a rapid-fire contribution of 97 put Burden back in the acendency and he secured his place in the final by taking the next frame.
> 
> Post-match, Burden said: “It was a tough game but I was pleased with the way I played and it stands me in good stead for the final. I’ve prepared well, practiced hard and I feel confident. I feel really strong – I’m going out and expecting to win tomorrow.”
> 
> ![Image 3](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-2.png?w=1024)
> 
> The second semi-final of the afternoon saw Canavan face Dale and, after sharing the first four frames of the contest, ‘The Spaceman’ appeared to step up a gear and fired in back-to-back century breaks of 109 and 131 before moving one frame from victory by taking the seventh.
> 
> The man from Jersey refused to go away, however, and managed to take the next three frames with a top visit of 65 to force an unlikely deciding frame.
> 
> ![Image 4](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-3.png?w=1024)
> 
> The decider was a nervy affair with both players spurning golden opportunities for the win. Ultimately, it was Canavan who took it on the colours to complete a famous comeback and set up a final meeting with Burden.
> 
> Canavan said: “It was tough. After last night, I was really tired but I gave myself a good talking to in the dressing room and came out fighting. It’s dream, you never think that you will get there and then all of a sudden something happens and you’re actually living the dream.”

The New Senior Snooker Season is upon us with some interesting changes
======================================================================

[July 16, 2025](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/07/16/the-new-senior-snooker-season-is-upon-us-with-some-interesting-changes/) [seniorsnooker](https://seniorsnooker.com/author/seniorsnooker/) [Uncategorized](https://seniorsnooker.com/category/uncategorized/)

This was announced by Jason Francis and [published on the WSS site](https://seniorssnooker.com/world-seniors-snooker-launches-new-season-with-increased-prize-money/):

> **World Seniors Snooker Launches New Season with Increased Prize Money  
> ****World Seniors Snooker (WSS) have today announced the dates for the 2025/26 season which will see nine tour events, with a minimum of four places available for players in their 2026 World Seniors Snooker Championship via the ranking list qualification system**
> ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> 
> Changes for the new campaign mean anyone over 40, including World Snooker Tour (WST) professionals, are now eligible to participate in the tour events which will see the winner’s prize doubled each weekend to £1,000 and prize money being paid down to the last 16.
> 
> ![Image 1](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/seniorswc2021sf-arena-1.jpeg?w=700)
> 
> Jason Francis, Chairman of WSS, said “_This season there are a lot more players eligible to play, including a number of WST professionals, and we have pledged £27,000 in prize money across our nine events which is more than double the amount that was on offer last season. If you are over 40, now is the time to dust off your cue and come and enjoy some friendly but serious competition_”
> 
> The season will begin on Friday 15 August  2025 with all events played at the Crucible Sports and Social Club in Reading.
> 
> TOUR DATES
> ----------
> 
> ### 2025
> 
> *   August 15-17
> *   September 26-28
> *   October 10-12
> *   November 21-23
> *   December 12-14
> 
> ### 2026
> 
> *   January 16-18
> *   February 6-8
> *   March 6-8
> *   April 3-5
> 
> On the Sunday of each weekend, a Super Seniors event will be staged for those aged over 55.
> 
> All events are now open for entry via [WPBSA SnookerScores](https://snookerscores.net/organisation/world-seniors-snooker/tournaments). A [WSS Tour membership](https://snookerscores.net/organisation/world-seniors-snooker/memberships) will be required in order to compete in the Race to the Crucible series.

The fact that players, including active professionals, are now eligible to compete on the Seniors Tour from the age of 40, instead of 45 in previous season, is a side effect of the failure of the negotiations between WST and Jason Francis, and one, I’m sure, that displeases WST much more than Jason…

How many active pros will be interested, and which ones, remains to be seen as they will have to set their priorities and find “spaces” in a rather full professional calendar. Another interesting question is wether the senior amateurs will feel excited at the prospect to play professionals and will embrace the challenge or if, on the contrary, this may be a deterrent if they feel that they have no chance to beat the pros.

All events will be played in Reading and that venue is very good but I remember the time, pre Brexit and pre covid, when some seniors qualifying events were played in mainland Europe. I wish it was still the case, but I guess, it would not be economically viable in the current state of affairs. It’s a shame though.

World Seniors Snooker Championship: 2025 draw, preview, schedule
================================================================

by [David Caulfield](https://snookerhq.com/author/snookerhq/ "Posts by David Caulfield") on May 7, 2025
